channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: Target Regeneration Shrinks the Gains of Draft-Training Objectives in Speculative Decoding
item.description: This is an evaluation-methodology finding, not a new decoding method: it replaces the standard practice of crediting draft-training objectives (token-level distillation, verification-gated distillation) with acceptance gains measured on externally written responses, requiring instead a baseline where the target model greedily regenerates the training corpus. The cost is one additional greedy inference pass of the target model over the corpus and retraining or re-evaluating drafters against the regenerated text, which is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU or via API. What can fail is overcorrecting: teams may discard distillation-based drafters that still help under real serving distributions, or regenerate with decoding settings that diverge from production, since the shrinkage's magnitude depends on the verifier and temperature regime. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: GRAM: Group-wise Rank-Aware Model Merging via Subspace Alignment
item.description: GRAM replaces single uniform SVD-based weight merging of fine-tuned task models with principal-angle-based task grouping followed by a standard SVD merge within each coalition. The cost is holding K merged models instead of one (K=2 doubles inference memory and serving footprint) plus an offline merge-time computation over fine-tuned weights only. It can fail when tasks do not form geometrically coherent groups, when per-group rank budgets are too tight, and it degrades to standard merging if K must be one due to deployment constraints. 1 independent implementation, 126 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Resuming Vision-Language Inference across Onboard Interruptions
item.description: It replaces naive restart-from-scratch inference after interruptions with phase-aware checkpointing (vision encoding, prefill, decoding) and dependency-aware partial-state recovery. It costs additional SSD write traffic, checkpoint storage, scheduling complexity, and a recovery-planning component that must integrate with the inference stack. It can fail if checkpoint overhead exceeds recomputation savings on rarely interrupted workloads, if storage or bandwidth is constrained, or if the scheduling model misestimates layer and token-chunk restore costs. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Understanding Target Probability Reuse in Speculative Decoding
item.description: It replaces draft-model ranking of the speculative token tree with reranking and first-token sampling based on a separately computed target-model distribution at the current context. It costs one additional target-model forward pass per round plus scheduling complexity to overlap that pass with drafting, and exact probability reuse may require discarding accepted tokens in unrestricted target models. It can fail if the extra target pass cannot be overlapped with drafting, since the added latency can erase the acceptance gains, and benefits shrink at large tree budgets. 2 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Cache Locally, Recompute Selectively for Streaming Video Understanding
item.description: FrameBlend replaces long-context idle-time prefill with short-window prefill plus query-time re-prefill of selected video tokens, whose recomputed KVs overwrite the stale cached entries. It costs an additional partial prefill pass at query time, adding latency and implementation complexity in token selection and cache replacement, though the paper reports this is outweighed by the prefill savings. It can fail when token selection misses query-relevant frames, when queries arrive too densely to amortize idle-time prefill, or with frameworks whose cache layouts do not support surgical KV replacement. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Credit Where Credit Is Due: Contrastive Attribution Topology Search for Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: CATS replaces score-only heuristic or random search over multi-agent topologies with LLM-attributed per-agent credit from contrasted execution traces, pruning weak edges and agents to yield a compact deployment team. The cost is an additional search phase: matched candidate evaluations across the supergraph plus LLM attributer calls, which adds offline token spend and implementation complexity before any deployment savings are realized. Credit assignment can fail when attributer judgments are noisy or confounded, traces do not isolate individual agent effects, or the pruned topology overfits the search benchmarks and underperforms on shifted production distributions. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Compressing Onboard Language Models for Space Robots under a Behavioral-Fidelity Requirement
item.description: It replaces choosing one post-training quantization family, or accepting implicit PTQ behavior, with per-linear-module selection among AWQ, GPTQ, and AutoRound checkpoints using final next-token KL against a BF16 reference. The cost is offline compression-time search, multiple compatible checkpoints, BF16 reference forward passes, optional labeled task data, and continued configuration control of a static artifact whose unquantized embedding/output layers are 43-46% at 3 bits. It can fail when general-domain KL/perplexity gains do not transfer to the production command distribution, when target-adapted selection overfits small labels, or when mixed-checkpoint compatibility and unquantized layers erode the expected memory and fidelity benefits. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: BrainCodes: A Lightweight EEG Foundation Model over Discrete Neural Codes
item.description: BrainCodes replaces large EEG foundation models with a compact architecture combining a quantization-based neural tokenizer and a spatiotemporal encoder supporting arbitrary electrode configurations, pretrained self-supervised on 800+ hours of EEG. The cost is domain specificity: it applies only to EEG pipelines and requires access to EEG data and task-specific fine-tuning, offering nothing for text or general multimodal workloads. Failure modes include degraded transfer to electrode montages or recording conditions outside the pretraining distribution and the general risk that an unreviewed arXiv preprint's cross-device claims do not hold on the reader's hardware or subjects. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
item.description: The framework proposes replacing passive retrieval-cache memory with a continual-learning view of agent memory, organized by substrates, assets, and policies with an inner state-update loop and an outer policy-refinement loop. It is a taxonomy plus evaluation and scaling methodology, so adoption costs engineering effort to redesign memory systems and evaluation pipelines, but it provides no concrete algorithm or implementation to deploy directly. It can fail to yield behavioral gains if memory writes are noisy or policies are not tuned, since the abstract reports no empirical results demonstrating that the approach improves future actions. 3 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories
item.description: OnQ replaces fixed-response teacher supervision in quantization-aware training with on-policy distillation, where the full-precision teacher supervises the quantized student on the student's own generated prefixes, weighted candidate-wise by Dynamic KL. It costs a full training pipeline rather than post-training calibration: student rollout generation plus teacher forward passes per step, which raises compute and implementation complexity beyond block-wise calibration alone. It can fail when the teacher itself is unreliable on student-generated prefixes, when budget limits prevent multiple QAT runs, and its results are demonstrated only on Qwen3 models up to 8B, so transfer to other families or larger scales is unverified. 2 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A KAN-based Non-linear Factorization for Embedding Layer Compression
item.description: It replaces the purely linear low-rank decomposition of an embedding matrix with a factorization that inserts learnable univariate (KAN-style) nonlinear projections inside the compressed embedding layer, optionally initialized from a pretrained uncompressed embedding and refined with distillation. The cost is additional per-parameter compute for the learnable univariate functions, extra implementation complexity over a standard two-matrix factorization, and a refinement/distillation phase to recover quality. It can fail because evidence is limited to Skip-gram word2vec-style embeddings on analogy and similarity benchmarks, so gains may not transfer to large transformer embedding tables, and KAN function evaluation may erode the latency and memory savings the compression was meant to provide. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Harness Scaling replaces agentic RL performed through a single fixed harness with RL conducted across a factorized, systematically sampled set of harness configurations, which the authors report improves generalization to unseen white-box and black-box harnesses. Its cost is substantial: it requires RL training runs across multiple harness configurations, repeated for several model scales and algorithms, which demands training compute, harness engineering, and evaluation infrastructure well beyond a single 24 GB GPU or API-only setup. Adoption can fail if the factorized harness space omits the dimensions that matter for a deployment harness, if the balanced factorial subset is too small to induce transfer, or if the reader's underlying API model cannot be fine-tuned at all, in which case the method is inapplicable. 4 independent implementations, 15 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RCSD: Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Domain-Specific Speculative Decoding
item.description: RCSD replaces soft-label distillation of the draft model with a reinforcement-style objective trained on accepted/rejected token pairs collected during speculative inference, optimizing acceptance length directly rather than distribution mimicry. The cost is a custom training pipeline: speculative decoding must already run in production to harvest preference pairs, plus masked-loss training infrastructure and continual updates as traffic shifts, though the resulting draft model remains small and inference-time memory is unchanged. It can fail if production traffic drifts from the training distribution (acceptance rates decay, requiring retraining cycles), if the small team cannot maintain the data-collection loop, or on workloads where speculative decoding itself offers little headroom (e.g., low-batch or highly deterministic generation). 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Stochastic Pruning of the DPO Computation Graph: 1.4x Faster Training and Lower Peak Memory
item.description: The method replaces the standard concatenated DPO training step with stochastic sampling of scored response positions, executed prefixes, and backpropagated preference branches, omitting the corresponding computation before it occurs. It costs a modified training objective (partially corrected with inverse-probability weighting for single-branch gradients), added implementation complexity in the training loop, and slightly lower mean accuracy with benchmark-dependent changes in open-ended generation scores. It can fail if the accuracy degradation is unacceptable for the target task, if the claimed savings do not transfer beyond the two model families evaluated, or if the unbiased estimator's higher variance destabilizes convergence on the reader's data distribution. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RISK-KV: Quality-Aware Selective KV Cache Reconstruction for Distributed LLM Inference
item.description: RISK-KV replaces full KV cache retention/transfer and full token replay during request migration and interruption recovery, reconstructing missing layers' KV states via cross-layer ridge regression folded into the model's projection matrices. It costs a topology search with quality gating, per-layer-group predictor fitting, storage for regression parameters, and a measured NLL degradation that must stay under the gating threshold. It can fail if reconstruction error exceeds the quality gate on out-of-distribution inputs, if the 512-token-history speedup does not generalize to longer contexts, or if the reader's workload lacks migration/recovery events frequent enough to amortize the search and fitting overhead. 1 independent implementation, 4 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
item.description: PACE replaces per-token rounding of the recurrent state in linear-attention and hybrid models (e.g., 8-bit DAMP or Q-Mamba) with post-hoc 4-bit quantization that rounds only once every few tokens, shares scales per column, and keeps error-sensitive heads at 8 bits. It requires a small token buffer between rounding points and mixed-precision head handling, adding modest kernel and serving complexity; accuracy on the 4B model is not fully preserved at 4 bits. Failure modes include quality degradation on smaller models, dependence on chunked-kernel serving stacks that support buffered decoding, and sensitivity to workloads dominated by long concurrent generations where state memory is not the actual bottleneck. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TernScope: Model-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient Ternary Endoscopic Segmentation
item.description: TernScope replaces full-precision or 8-bit convolutional segmentation with a co-designed ternary-weight (W2/A8) network trained via progressive quantization-aware training from deep to shallow layers. The claimed gains (multiplier-free compute, packed storage, 88.46% area reduction) materialize only on custom systolic-array silicon; on a 24 GB GPU, ternary weights provide no practical speed or memory benefit without specialized kernels, and the model is already small enough that deployment constraints are unlikely to bind. Failure modes include accuracy loss on out-of-domain endoscopy data from aggressive quantization, engineering cost of the TPQ pipeline, and the fact that none of the hardware advantages transfer to commodity GPU inference. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Effects of Model Scale and Quantization on Social Bias and Abstention in Question Answering
item.description: It replaces single-metric fairness checks (counting biased responses on BBQ) with a joint evaluation that tracks bias, abstention rate, prompt formulation, and answer-option design together when selecting model size and quantization settings. It costs only additional evaluation passes on existing benchmarks and forces disclosure of over-abstention, adding modest evaluation compute and reporting complexity. It can fail if BBQ results are treated as representative of production distributions, since the paper shows trends are not stable across prompt formulations, model families, or forced-choice settings, so conclusions may not transfer. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: SPARE: Sparsity Allocation via Routing Entropy for Efficient MoEs
item.description: SPARE replaces uniform per-layer expert pruning budgets with a layer-wise allocation derived from routing entropy measured on calibration data, applied on top of any existing expert selector. It is training-free, so its cost is a calibration forward pass and the engineering of pruning and remapping experts; the pruned model is smaller in memory but loses capacity relative to the dense model. It can fail when calibration data is unrepresentative of production traffic, since routing entropy estimates then misallocate the pruning budget, and gains shrink at low pruning ratios where uniform allocation is already adequate. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Uni-Mem: Learning a Long-Horizon Agentic Memory Manager with Unified Online Policy Optimization
item.description: Replaces hand-designed memory workflows and hybrid RL-plus-offline-supervision pipelines with a single policy trained end-to-end online for both memory construction and retrieval, using stage-decoupled group comparisons and event-level credit assignment. Costs include an online RL training loop over long memory trajectories, the added complexity of alternating stage optimization, and dependence on RL-quality reward signals; the abstract gives no compute or latency figures. Can fail if rewards are sparse or misaligned, if benchmarks like LoCoMo do not transfer to the reader's workloads, or if the trained policy is brittle under distribution shift in production interactions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Benchmarking Coding Agents for System-Level Performance Optimization
item.description: This benchmark replaces ad hoc or function-level evaluation of coding agents with 65 reproducible system-level optimization instances across seven microservice systems, each with executable environments, functional tests, and mixed-workload measurement. The cost is infrastructure effort: each instance requires a runnable multi-service environment and workload harness, which is heavier than typical function-level benchmarks though feasible on a single machine or modest cloud budget. It can fail to predict production behavior because the anti-patterns are synthetically injected rather than observed in real incidents, so agent scores may not transfer to organically occurring bottlenecks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
item.description: This replaces closed-book answering and naive claim-as-query single-shot retrieval with a ReAct-style agent that writes its own search queries against a live retrieval API, and it replaces existence-only citation checks with relevance auditing. The cost is multi-turn tool interaction (more latency and API calls than single-shot, though agents used under half their search budget) plus harness complexity; the backbone and output format need not change. It can fail silently through plausible but irrelevant citations: closed-book models produced real PubMed IDs that were relevant in only 3 of 327 cases, so PMID existence checks give false assurance, and the accuracy gains are not statistically significant, so benefits must be validated on your workload. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: UlaCache: Unified Logical Addressing for Sparse LLM Serving
item.description: UlaCache replaces conventional physically-tied KV cache management with a unified logical address space spanning GPU and optional CPU memory, combined with a Parallel Bucketed LRU for shared GPU pool eviction, so sparse-attention KV selection is decoupled from physical placement. The cost is substantial systems complexity: address-mapping infrastructure, CPU-GPU transfer coordination, local buffer management across decoding steps, and integration with sparse attention and speculative decoding, with gains demonstrated only on H200 and B300 hardware in DP/TP configurations. It can fail when the workload does not already use sparse attention and speculative decoding, when transfer bandwidth between CPU and GPU becomes the bottleneck, or when the reader's single 24 GB GPU cannot realize the distributed-storage benefits the system is designed around. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory
item.description: It replaces pre-question memory extraction systems such as Mem0 and Zep, and partly full-context prompting, by keeping the raw conversation history and letting a capable model search it with agent tools at query time. It eliminates the memory-writing pipeline and its build cost, but shifts spend to per-query tool-using rollouts whose cost and latency depend on the model and retrieval loop. It can fail because the advantage rests on a strong reader model and on agent-readable artifacts such as photo captions, and with weaker models designed memory still wins; the evidence base is one conversation with one run per cell. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
item.description: HAWK replaces single-device-type serving with phase-disaggregated inference in which prefill runs on GPUs and decode on NPUs, connected by an RDMA path that remaps KV cache tensor layouts into NPU-side layout-aware buffers during transfer. It costs dedicated heterogeneous hardware (commercial NPUs plus RDMA-capable interconnect), custom transfer orchestration, and up to 7.88% throughput loss relative to a GPU-only baseline. It can fail through cross-device layout mismatches, RDMA path or interconnect instability, and engineering fragility when models, KV formats, or hardware generations change. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Robust Soft Skill Adaptation via Behavioral Localization in Tool-Using Agents
item.description: The method replaces supervising soft prompts on entire successful trajectories (or passing long text skills at inference) with supervision restricted to trajectory positions where the text skill both raises the likelihood of successful tokens and shifts the next-token distribution. It costs extra frozen-model forward passes, with and without the skill, to score every position before training, and adds a localization pipeline on top of standard soft-prompt training. It can fail when skill effects are diffuse rather than concentrated, when the localization threshold or top-k fraction is miscalibrated for a new domain, or when gains measured on a single benchmark (SpreadsheetBench, one frozen model) do not transfer to the reader's tasks. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: From Reasoning to Action: Benchmarking Frontier AI Models on LIBERO-10 Robot Manipulation Tasks
item.description: The approach replaces task-specific manipulation training or pretrained skill policies with direct closed-loop control by a frontier multimodal model issuing end-effector poses and gripper commands. It costs per-episode API inference that scales with reasoning effort, requires a physical or simulated robot stack, and adds integration complexity for vision, proprioception, and tool-call handling. With a best success rate of 44% and weakness on precise spatial and multi-step tasks, it fails on reliability-critical deployments and offers no guaranteed recovery when a subtask misfires. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: From Classifier Heads to Encoder Prototypes: Personalized Federated Learning with Head-Derived Clustering
item.description: HDC-FL replaces separate clustered-FL objectives and second optimization trajectories by clustering clients using their own classifier heads, then returning a soft mixture of per-cluster encoder prototypes while keeping client heads private. Its cost is a periodic server-side projection, clustering, and prototype-construction step plus cached client encoders and heads; it does not reduce client compute, memory, or communication. It can fail when head similarity does not track encoder compatibility (the paper itself finds this association weakest outside covariate shift), and its evidence is limited to CIFAR-10/100 with ResNet-18 and MobileNetV2, with no quantified gain factor reported. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
item.description: This survey introduces PAPAV, a taxonomy that replaces architecture-specific comparisons of computer-use and robot-use agents with five functional capabilities (Perceive, Anticipate, Plan, Act, Verify), so it is an analytical lens rather than a deployable method. It costs nothing to run but offers no model, code, or benchmark improvement; its value is limited to framing evaluation and design. Its survey finding that only 5 of 64 benchmarks assess Anticipate and 3 assess Verify indicates current agent evaluations over-weight task success, but adopting the framework cannot itself close those gaps and may not map cleanly onto an engineer's existing evaluation harness. 4 independent implementations, 371 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: The End of Consensus Research?
item.description: The method replaces manual expert-driven consensus protocol design and evaluation with an agent harness combining a protocol knowledge base, a modular implementation skeleton, and Lean-based formal verification. It costs substantial domain-specific scaffolding (knowledge base, reusable Lean specifications and proofs, evaluation infrastructure) plus expert oversight, rather than GPU or inference budget. The discovered protocol's gains apply only to geo-replicated state machines, and the paper itself shows agents can surface but also miss correctness issues, since its Lean formalization exposed previously unreported vulnerabilities in existing protocols. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
item.description: It replaces static, single-role agent benchmarks with a dynamic pairwise protocol in which models both author hint-gated environments and solve those written by other models, separating authoring skill from solving skill. Adoption costs the API spend to run multiple frontier models across generated environments plus integration of the released harness, and the abstract reports no quantified latency, memory, or accuracy improvement for the adopting engineer. It can fail as a selection signal because rankings reflect this specific duel format, smaller models authored the hardest environments, and hint-lift correlation with held-out benchmark gains is demonstrated only for a single RL study on one model. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LoRASpace: A Pool-Wide Shared Substrate for Static and Dynamic Multi-LoRA Composition
item.description: It replaces either lossy multi-LoRA weight merging or one-forward-pass-per-LoRA composite inference with a shared low-rank subspace computed once per adapter pool. The cost is an offline SVD over the pool, storage and bookkeeping for the shared basis, plus extra routing logic for dynamic mode; it is training-free at inference time. It can fail when the pool has little rank overlap, as in the diversity-curated LoRA-Retriever benchmark near 96% of summed rank, and the ablation indicates the static quality gain may come from rank allocation rather than the pool-wide basis itself. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: KatoANN: Enabling Near-Exact Vector Search at the Speed of Lossy Scans with CPU Matrix Engines
item.description: The method replaces memory-bound lossy distance scans (or a full-vector refinement pass) in partition-family ANN search with a batched rank-then-refine scan over a single 16-bit SQ16 code, using Intel AMX to reuse fetched codes across queries. Costs include 16-bit storage per vector plus the rank-refine scan logic, and it depends on Intel AMX CPU hardware and on batch query availability to shift the workload from memory-bound to compute-bound. It can fail under low query concurrency, where batching yields little reuse, on hardware without AMX, or on workloads where SQ16 high-byte ranking misidentifies survivors and recall degrades. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TeCoP: Accelerating Diffusion Large Language Model Decoding via Tentative Context Pipelining
item.description: TeCoP replaces the serialized block-wise decoder of diffusion LLMs (LLaDA, Dream) with a training-free staggered block-parallel pipeline that reuses stable but uncommitted predictions as provisional context, committing them via confidence and stability checks in a draft-and-verify loop. It costs implementation complexity in the decoding loop and carries the accuracy risk of committing tokens conditioned on provisional context that later proves wrong, though reported accuracy stays within one point of the original decoder. It can fail on workloads where low-confidence or unstable early predictions propagate errors across blocks, and it applies only to diffusion LLMs, not autoregressive models. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Radiation-Hardened, Fault-Aware Quantized Neural Network That Self-Heals
item.description: The method replaces extra weight replicas and classical SECDED ECC for repairing bit-flipped quantized weights, by training with a low-rank alignment penalty and reconstructing corrupted coordinates from uncorrupted ones at runtime. Its costs are a modified Fault-Aware Training procedure with an added alignment penalty, runtime projection computation during healing, and an accepted RMSE degradation of +5% to +50% depending on scrub interval. It can fail if corruption exceeds what the low-rank subspace can reconstruct from surviving coordinates, and it is validated only on six small regression benchmarks rather than production-scale models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: SliMOO: Interpretable Multi-Objective Evolutionary Search for LLM Depth Pruning
item.description: SliMOO replaces single-score layer-importance ranking and greedy or scalarized depth pruning with a two-stage procedure: single-layer removal probing to build a task-layer importance map, followed by NSGA-II Pareto-aware evolutionary search over pruning masks scored by per-task deviation from the dense model. The cost is substantial offline search compute, since each candidate mask requires multi-task evaluation of the full model, plus added pipeline complexity relative to one-shot importance ranking; the pruned model itself reduces serving memory and latency proportionally to removed layers. It can fail when the evaluation tasks used during search do not represent production traffic, since the method optimizes deviation only on chosen benchmarks, and the evolutionary search may not transfer across model families or sparsity targets without re-running. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ProVe: Proposer-Verifier Decoding
item.description: ProVe replaces the standard speculative-decoding arrangement (small serial drafter, large parallel verifier) by fine-tuning the large AR model to propose a block of future tokens in one forward pass, then verifying with a second pass from itself or a small model. It costs a fine-tuning run on the large checkpoint, one extra forward pass per block, and, in the lossy variant, a measurable accuracy drop (about 2.6 points on the reported six-task average); the lossless variant adds verification compute but preserves greedy AR outputs. It can fail if proposed blocks have short AR-matching prefixes on the target workload (gains depend on the 6.6-of-16 prefix statistic holding), if the fine-tune degrades base-model quality, or if self-verification overhead erodes the speedup at small batch sizes. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: From Tokens to Files: Multi-Granularity Detection and Localization of AI-Involved Code
item.description: Replaces file-level single-score AI-code detectors (stylistic features or global code embeddings) with per-token log-likelihood ratios from two low-rank adapters on a frozen code LM, aggregated to line, block, and file decisions. Cost is modest: a frozen code model plus two LoRA adapters and lightweight aggregation heads fits a single 24 GB GPU, but requires training data of paired human and AI-generated or AI-modified files across generation regimes, which the reader must construct or obtain. Can fail under generator drift (models unlike the training counterparts), on heavily post-edited AI code where local evidence is diluted, and the internal 72.4 F1 may not transfer since the external benchmark result is lower and only line-level. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ACE-Compression: An Ability-Centric Evaluation of Compressed Large Language Models
item.description: Replaces aggregate task-score evaluation of quantized or pruned checkpoints with a diagnostic framework probing four ability dimensions: procedural reasoning, knowledge grounding, social cognition, and persona fidelity. Cost is additional evaluation compute per checkpoint and integration of a new benchmark suite, with no change to model memory or serving latency. It can fail if its ability probes do not match the reader's actual workload distribution, leading to a compression choice optimized for the framework's dimensions rather than the application's real failure modes. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Training the Whole Agent, Not Just the Model
item.description: The method replaces a fixed, human-designed agent harness with tools, hooks, and task-specific skills evolved by frozen teacher models alongside GRPO policy training, and its deployment artifact is the trained model plus the evolved harness. The full pipeline costs RL training of a 9B policy, teacher-model inference for skill and tool generation, and an accept-reject loop gated on observed pass rate and trainable rate, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU; the harness-evolution component alone is API-feasible. Failure modes include harness overfitting to training tasks (the paper itself reports up to 7.7 points lost if the evolved harness is removed at deployment), acceptance decisions driven by noisy pass-rate estimates, and tool changes that help the current policy but degrade as the policy drifts. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MuPACE: Learning to Pace Muon for LoRA Fine-Tuning
item.description: MuPACE replaces per-problem learning rate schedule tuning for LoRA fine-tuning with a small recurrent policy that adjusts the step size of an otherwise untouched Muon optimizer on top of an interpretable analytic schedule. The cost is the meta-training phase across a distribution of fine-tuning runs plus an extra recurrent controller in the training loop, though inference and the deployed adapter are unaffected. It can fail when the production task or model distribution differs sharply from the meta-training distribution, when the meta-training budget is unavailable to a small team, or when the claimed transfer does not hold for non-Qwen architectures or non-LoRA configurations. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ClawMMU: Protection-Coherent Virtual Memory for Stateful LLM Agents
item.description: Replaces implicit trust in agent long-term memory with explicit labels recording owner, scope, origin, and authority, checked whenever content enters context, is stored, is retrieved, or triggers a tool call, turning prompt-injection attacks into protection faults. Costs harness engineering effort and metadata bookkeeping on every memory operation, plus some added latency per check; no model retraining or extra GPU capacity is required. It can fail through mislabeled provenance at ingestion, incomplete coverage of an unmonitored channel, or an over-restrictive policy that blocks legitimate memory use, and the abstract provides no measured attack-reduction or overhead figures. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AgenTest: Mining Business Rules to Test LLM Agents for Business Logic Bugs
item.description: AgenTest replaces manual business-rule test writing and success-only or policy-based agent evaluation with automatic mining of system prompts, tool definitions, and domain knowledge into Given-When-Then specifications, each exercised via multi-turn interactions and a hybrid oracle over messages, tool calls, and state. The cost is the engineering to build satisfying environment states and simulated users per specification, plus LLM and orchestration expense for multi-turn test execution; the paper shows no turnkey tool, so adoption means reimplementing the pipeline. It can fail where rules remain implicit and unmined, where environment instantiation is infeasible for real production systems, or where the hybrid oracle misjudges ambiguous traces, producing false positives or missed violations. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment for LLM Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
item.description: TEPCA replaces standard semantic-relevance RAG retrieval and fixed, input-agnostic LoRA adapters with time-constrained path pruning plus mutual-information fact filtering, and a timestamp-gated LoRA that modulates the adaptation subspace per temporal context. The cost is a more complex retrieval pipeline (graph path construction, MI scoring, temporal constraints) and training the DG-LoRA gating mechanism, adding latency and engineering overhead beyond off-the-shelf RAG. It can fail if the underlying TKG has sparse or noisy timestamps, if queries lack clear temporal grounding, or if the extra pruning discards evidence that simpler retrieval would have kept. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Offline Makes Online Better: Calibrated Cache Compression for Video Generation
item.description: CALM replaces uniform-ratio token merging in KV-cache compression for autoregressive video generation with a fixed layer-head merging allocation, selected offline via an attention-output error proxy and applied at inference through dynamic programming under a given cache budget. The cost is a one-time offline calibration per model, plus dependence on the assumption that attention-output error predicts end-to-end video quality; inference overhead itself is minimal once the risk map is built. It can fail if the calibrated sensitivity map does not transfer to new prompts, model versions, or cache budgets far from those used in calibration, and the 21% LPIPS gain is reported against the method's own uniform-merging baseline, not against uncompressed generation. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
item.description: Replaces training target-specific forecasting models from scratch and avoids the memory and compute cost of full fine-tuning of a pretrained time series foundation model. Costs roughly 1% of model parameters in trainable weights plus labeled target-domain data, with quality that varies by model family and target series. Can fail when the pretrained checkpoint is already strong for the target (as with Chronos-2), when OOD targets show no adaptation gain, or when target data is too scarce to tune even low-rank adapters. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MaD-RSI: Model-as-Data for Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
item.description: MaD-RSI replaces single-model recursive self-improvement of agent harnesses, in which a harness is overfit to one LLM and must be re-optimized per model, with joint optimization of one shared harness using failure trajectories from several heterogeneous LLMs. The cost is a more complex training pipeline that must run and collect trajectories from multiple models during optimization, plus API or inference spend for each participating model, which is non-trivial even if lower than per-model re-optimization. It can fail if the shared harness converges to an average that underperforms a model-specific harness on the reader's actual production model, if the reader only uses one or two models (removing the diversity signal the method depends on), or if trajectory collection across API providers is rate-limited or expensive. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Forty Questions: Identifying a Language Model from One-Word Answers
item.description: The method replaces trusting provider labels or running heavyweight benchmark suites to verify which model an API endpoint actually serves, using a public census of default one-word answers and likelihood-based attribution. It costs cents per endpoint, requires no GPU, and adds only a small profiling script plus a reference answer database to the engineering stack. It can fail when a system prompt is injected (accuracy drops 6 to 16 points), when reasoning modes or provider-side context injection alter default answers, and it cannot resolve every endpoint, as two of 96 remained unidentified. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ChartEvo: Self-Evolving Agent Harnesses for Long-Tail Chart Reasoning
item.description: It replaces manually engineered per-chart-type strategies and tools with a recursive framework that evolves reusable skills, executable tools, and tool-call chains driven by observed failures. It costs additional inference overhead from tool-augmented reasoning (partially controlled via learned local tool-call chains), plus the engineering complexity of maintaining an evolving skill and tool library around an API-based MLLM. It can fail if the self-improvement loop overfits to the evaluation distribution, if evolved tools are unreliable or unsafe to execute, and the reported gains are validated only on two chart benchmarks with a single proprietary base model. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
item.description: Replaces ad hoc, empirically designed multi-agent collaboration protocols with a block-coordinate scheme in which agents propose local edits with cross-part corrections and a coordinator merges proposals only after checking them against a global objective. Costs include extra coordinator inference per round, correction-computation overhead, and implementation complexity, all multiplied by the number of API or model calls across agents. Can fail when local corrections are inaccurate (raising the error floor), when proposals frequently interfere and combination checks reject them, or on tasks without a decomposable global objective, where the protocol adds cost without convergence benefit. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Disclosure Begets Disclosure: A Self-Reinforcing Privacy Loop in LLM Agents with Persistent Memory
item.description: The technique replaces memory-write filtering and storage anonymization with a response-level instruction that prevents the agent from stating or presupposing stored personal attributes, breaking a self-reinforcing disclosure loop in persistent-memory agents. It costs only a system-prompt change and a small loss of personalization quality relative to full memory use, far less than the quality loss from filtering user input or stored content. It can fail if the instruction is not followed reliably across models or sessions, if inference-based leakage occurs without explicit presupposition, or if the simulated-user findings do not transfer to real user behavior. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
item.description: It replaces single-pass VLM spatial answering and specialized spatial-reasoning systems with an off-the-shelf general coding agent (e.g., Codex, Claude Code) wired to a command-line 3D perception toolkit, a persistent scene memory, and plain-language interpretation of tool readings. The cost is multi-turn agent-loop latency, increased token and API spend from iterative tool calls, and engineering effort to build and maintain the perception toolkit and memory layer, with no model training required. After adoption, gains can shrink as backbone models improve (the paper itself reports diminishing tool benefits), agent loops can misinterpret correct tool outputs or compound errors across steps, and results depend on the coverage and geometric accuracy of the perception tools in the target environment. 3 independent implementations, 144 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond the Point Mass: Acceptance-Derived Weights and Distributional Losses for Speculative Decoding
item.description: It replaces the point-mass cross-entropy drafter loss and D-PACE's position weights with overlap-derived (TV-based) acceptance weights and a Rényi-1/2 divergence loss during drafter training. It costs only a modification to the drafter training objective, roughly a 1.5% acceptance-length gain, and no inference-time changes, extra memory, or additional models. It can fail if the gains do not transfer beyond the Qwen3-4B setting tested, if the draft and target distributions are poorly matched so the divergence signal is noisy, or if a 1.5% acceptance improvement does not justify retraining an existing drafter pipeline. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FALCA: Falsification-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Deep Search Agents
item.description: Replaces single-agent iterative deep search with a propose-falsify loop in which independent Falsifier agents seek counterevidence and revise the research state, optionally reinforced by SFT warmup and RL with hierarchical credit assignment. The inference-time cost is roughly doubled LLM calls per step plus orchestration overhead, and the training component requires parallel rollouts and staged reward assignment that are expensive on a 24 GB GPU and likely only feasible via third-party APIs. The loop can fail if Falsifiers share the backbone's blind spots and rubber-stamp candidates, if falsification reports are noisy enough to destabilize the research state, or if hierarchical credit assignment misattributes rewards across stages. 3 independent implementations, 134 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design
item.description: OO-Harness replaces a single global agent harness (fixed prompts, tools, and control flow) with an evolved hierarchy of specialized harness subclasses selected per task by a router trained on execution records. The cost is an offline evolution phase in which an evolution agent runs tasks and generates/refines harness code, adding API spend and engineering complexity, though test-time routing itself is lightweight. It can fail when the router misclassifies tasks, when evolved harnesses overfit the training task distribution and generalize poorly to new task types, or when the evolution budget is too small to discover useful specializations. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies
item.description: RACE replaces full-dimensional per-head keys and queries (and reconstruction-based KV-cache compression) with a natively reduced-dimensional attention formed by selecting complete RoPE rotary pairs ranked by joint query-key activation energy, folding the selection into the model weights post-training. It costs a one-time calibration pass and permanently removes up to half of the head dimension, trading some representational capacity for lower KV-cache memory and attention FLOPs without custom kernels. It can fail if the calibration set is unrepresentative of production inputs, if accuracy on zero-shot or long-context tasks degrades at the chosen compression level, or if short-context workloads see little benefit since the gains concentrate at long contexts. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: VisualEvolve: A Skill Self-Evolution Framework for Visual Reasoning
item.description: Replaces reinforcement-learning fine-tuning of tool-use behavior with an external, evolving library of executable visual skills selected and refined through a Select-Execute-Evolve-Evaluate loop, with snapshot selection and progressive evidence access to control regressions. Cost is inference-time API or GPU compute for trajectory generation, skill evaluation on a held-out validation set, and engineering effort to maintain the skill library and evolution harness rather than model training. Failures include skill regressions propagating if snapshot selection is misconfigured, evolution driven by non-representative validation tasks, and accumulated API or compute spend when many evolution cycles are needed. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
item.description: MAS-Guard replaces fragmented, single-threat defenses with a two-layer framework: per-agent task-specific guardrail experts (A-Guard) plus a system-level Control Plane enforcing developer-owned Agent Charters through deterministic route, capability, and message-format checks combined with semantic role and content assessment, with interventions of allow, reflection, confirmation, and block. It costs additional inference calls for the guardrail experts and semantic checks on agentic events, added latency per inter-agent message, and the engineering effort of authoring charters and deploying a control plane around existing agents. It can fail against opaque or compromised agents that bypass instrumentable layers, through semantic-check false positives that degrade benign-task utility, and against attack classes outside its six evaluation benchmarks. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: After the Attacker Leaves: Benchmarking Carryover Attacks on LLM Agents
item.description: This is an evaluation benchmark, not a deployable technique; it replaces single-session prompt-injection testing with multi-round measurement of memory-resident and scheduled-task payload re-firing. Running its 101 tasks against your agent costs API calls and engineering time, and the actionable finding is that defenses must sit at the runtime layer (memory-write gating, scheduled-task review) rather than in prompts. It can fail to transfer if your agent lacks persistent memory or heartbeat scheduling, and results on five frontier models may not predict behavior of the specific model and runtime you deploy. 4 independent implementations, 156 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Asymmetric Looped Transformers: Fixed Global Representations for an Iterative Decoder
item.description: It replaces full-stack layer looping, where one shared recurrent block both builds context and refines state, with a single-pass causal encoder producing fixed global KV caches plus a weight-tied recurrent decoder attending jointly to global and local KV. The cost is an architecture change requiring training from scratch, including a heavy-tail-guided layerwise learning-rate schedule, and some extra memory for per-layer global KV caches; there is no inference-time drop-in benefit. It can fail if the fixed-context/separate-refinement gains do not transfer beyond the FineWeb-Edu pretraining regime tested, and the absolute quality gain (~1.3 accuracy points) is modest relative to retraining cost. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Model- and Layer-Level Closed-Loop Forecasting with SSM-Based Spiking Neural Networks
item.description: The method replaces zero-masking or external autoregressive feed-in during the forecasting phase by feeding the network's own predictions back as inputs, at either model level or layer level. The cost is added architectural and training complexity in a spiking/Deep-SSM stack with limited tooling, plus a quality trade-off between continuous and low-bit quantized spike activations. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on the small ETT-small benchmark at parity with existing methods, so there is no evidence of advantage on larger, noisier production forecasting workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DecisionPivot: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Decision Models in LLM Systems
item.description: DecisionPivot replaces reliance on aggregate item accuracy for selecting and validating the decision models used for routing, guardrails, and output verification, substituting contrast-group accuracy, probability ordering, calibration, and selective-coverage diagnostics. Adoption costs evaluation engineering effort: running model-specific protocols across the benchmark's tracks and integrating the metrics into a selection pipeline, with no model training or additional GPU demand beyond inference. It can fail to transfer if the reader's production decision tasks differ from the 13 generated task families, and rankings may shift as models or reasoning-effort settings change. 3 independent implementations, 145 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Binary Discrete Diffusion: Candidate-Set Diffusion for Logic and Planning Tasks
item.description: It replaces masked and uniform discrete-diffusion corruption kernels with a candidate-set state (a binary membership vector per position) that changes through gradual additions and removals, explicitly representing partial uncertainty during iterative generation. It costs a new training and sampling stack rather than an off-the-shelf API model, since the reader would need to train or fine-tune task-specific diffusion models on a single 24 GB GPU, and adds kernel and sampler complexity relative to standard masked diffusion. It can fail because the demonstrated wins are confined to small structured logic and planning benchmarks at modest scale, gains may not transfer to general LLM reasoning or coding workloads, and per-position set representations raise memory and compute per step compared with single-token states. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Learning Computational Structure for Sample-Efficient Prediction
item.description: LeWi replaces fully dense MLP connectivity with wiring learned jointly with weights, where each neuron has a low-dimensional embedding and only nearby neurons connect. It adds embedding parameters and a locality-constrained training procedure, with modest implementation complexity over a standard dense network. It can fail on targets dominated by a single high-arity function, where dense networks perform better, and the evidence comes from controlled synthetic benchmarks and world-model prediction tasks rather than standard production workloads. 1 independent implementation, 217 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Large Flow Language Models
item.description: The method replaces standard single-token AR decoding with blockwise parallel flow generation plus in-model self-speculative verification, eliminating the need for a separate draft model. The cost is a specialized training procedure that adapts a pretrained AR checkpoint into a flow model (demonstrated at 0.5B–8B with under 30B tokens), which exceeds the reader's compute budget, plus added inference complexity for blockwise asynchronous decoding and prefix caching. It can fail if pretrained flow checkpoints are not released for the reader's domain, if the 2.54x speedup does not transfer to other base models or workloads, or if quality degrades at aggressive few-step generation settings. 3 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws
item.description: OptScientist replaces manual theory building and conventional symbolic regression by inferring compact symbolic optimization problems from data and wrapping the model in an LLM agent that supplies literature priors and proposes new experiments. It costs an agentic LLM pipeline (API spend or a hosted model), a custom-trained inference model, and an iterative data-collection loop rather than a single offline fit. It can fail when the true phenomenon is not well modeled as optimization, when the symbolic search overfits small datasets, or when literature priors bias discovery toward plausible but incorrect laws. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Cache Engineering for Agents
item.description: It replaces context-engineering approaches (trimming or summarizing history, which invalidates the prefix and forces re-prefill) with direct KV cache operations, drop and repos, that control active cache without altering the trajectory. The cost is operational: you must run or integrate the AKV serving engine to manage stateful cache reuse, eviction, and restoration, which excludes third-party API-only deployments and adds a serving-layer dependency. Failure modes include incorrect cache reuse from history dependence (identical token sequences with different cache states), potential accuracy loss if aggressive drop policies remove needed context, and policy fragility since gains depend on the workload-specific drop policy. 2 independent implementations, 142 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
item.description: The method replaces single-agent, single-pass long-horizon execution with a 35B MoE model that decomposes tasks, delegates to isolated-context subagents running in parallel, and verifies progress through evidence validation and reflective strategy revision. The cost is substantial: a 35B MoE exceeds comfortable serving on a single 24 GB GPU without aggressive quantization, so practical use implies third-party API spend or degraded local deployment, plus the orchestration layer adds system complexity and multiplied token consumption per task. Failure modes include unproductive delegation loops, verification that latches onto flawed evidence, runaway API costs on exploratory tasks, and unverifiable claims since the abstract reports no quantitative benchmark results. 1 independent implementation, 122 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
item.description: The method replaces hand-designed tool interfaces and hand-written usage knowledge for computer-use agents with a repository of interfaces that a meta-agent constructs from unlabeled task trajectories and selects via population-based evolution on held-out validation tasks. The cost is the offline evolution pipeline itself: many synthetic training tasks, full agent rollouts, and a meta-agent pass per iteration, which is significant API or GPU spend even though inference with the resulting repository adds little overhead. What can fail is generalization: interfaces evolved on synthetic tasks may not transfer to the reader's real applications, the open-source repository may be tuned to OSWorld-style benchmarks, and running custom evolution on a single 24 GB GPU with a small budget is likely impractical. 3 independent implementations, 12802 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TraceLite: Efficient Trace Reduction for SWE Agents via Optical Compression and Redundancy Removal
item.description: TraceLite replaces full-text retention of SWE-agent interaction histories, and compression methods that rely on model training or auxiliary LLM calls, with a pipeline that keeps recent observations as text, renders older observations as images, removes cross-step overlap, and discards payloads that expire after code editing. It costs only local rendering and image-encoding overhead (0.438 s per observation), but increases prompt image-token usage and implementation complexity in the agent loop. It can fail when vision encoders lose fidelity on dense or unusual text, when task phases are misdetected so needed payloads are discarded, and its gains may not transfer beyond the two evaluated frontier backbones and benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Weight Placement Is Not Enough: Synchronization in Multi-Node CPU Decoding of Ternary LLMs
item.description: The method replaces weight-placement-only NUMA optimization in multi-node CPU decoding with a redesign that cuts inter-thread barrier waits, using a Megatron-style column split without cross-node reductions on top of ik_llama.cpp kernels. Its cost is implementation complexity in a custom decode engine and it applies only to ternary-quantized models; the reader would also need dual-socket, multi-NUMA-node Xeon-class servers. It can fail outside its tested regime: gains shrink when decoding is not DRAM-bound, when models fit in L3 cache, and on single-socket or GPU-based deployments where the synchronization pattern does not apply. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Token-Set Choice Confounds POPE: A Systematic Audit of Yes/No Extraction in VLM Hallucination Evaluation
item.description: It replaces hard-coded vocabulary-ID yes/no comparisons in POPE-style logit readouts with a tokenizer-derived token set covering the surface forms the model actually emits (e.g., ' Yes' vs 'Yes'). The cost is a one-time audit of generated tokens per model/tokenizer plus a slightly larger lookup set; no additional memory, latency, or compute in production. It can fail if adopted naively: tokenizer readouts must still be re-derived per model family, and cross-paper score comparisons remain invalid until readout and quantization precision are matched, since measured baseline shifts exceeded most published mitigation gains. 4 independent implementations, 2 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Federated Community Detection in Bipartite Networks
item.description: FLICKER replaces centralized spectral decomposition of a horizontally partitioned matrix with federated power iteration that exchanges only matrix-vector products on local blocks, and BiFLICKER applies this to bipartite community detection. The cost is iterative cross-server communication rounds, a recursive grid search for spectral targets, and reliance on a reference server whose rescaled leading singular values must be valid global targets. It can fail when local sample sizes are too small for the reference server to estimate targets, when the data do not follow the assumed sparse bipartite stochastic block model, or when the horizontal partitioning assumption does not match the deployment. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: MX-Like Tensor Core for LLM Inference with NPU Integration via Hardware-Software Co-Design Exploration
item.description: The work does not replace a software technique; it replaces ad hoc selection of block-scaled quantization formats (OCP MX, NVFP4) with a systematic HW-SW co-design exploration of scale, weight, and activation format combinations on a specialized NPU MAC datapath. For a software practitioner the actionable finding is narrow: scale format choice matters mainly under aggressive FP4 quantization, where UE5M3 scales improve accuracy at negligible silicon cost. Adoption fails at the reader's constraints because the gains are realized only in custom NPU silicon (SNAX platform), cannot be enabled on a commodity 24 GB GPU or third-party API, and the perplexity results may not transfer across models or calibration pipelines. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Multilingual Voicemail and Answering Machine Detection via Pretrained Audio Embeddings and Gradient Boosting Machines
item.description: The method replaces proprietary answering machine detection systems and computationally expensive real-time models (including ASR-plus-LLM pipelines) with frozen pretrained audio embeddings feeding a gradient boosting classifier. Cost is low: no GPU or fine-tuning is required for inference, training reduces to fitting a GBM on extracted embeddings, and the authors release a 500+ recording, 7-language dataset (OpenAMD) for replication. What can fail: the dataset is small for a production telephony system, per-language and per-gender performance differences were found statistically significant, and robustness degrades under additive noise and packet loss typical of real carrier networks. 2 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Reliable Before Profitable: QuantHarness for Governing Financial Strategy Development with LLM Agents
item.description: It replaces ad-hoc single-agent or loosely scripted LLM pipelines for turning natural-language research requests into backtested financial strategies, substituting a structured workflow (specification, data grounding, construction, testing, review) with enforced stage-level information, action, and commitment boundaries. The cost is additional orchestration complexity, structured run-record storage, and extra LLM calls across stages, which raises latency and API spend per strategy developed. What can fail: the benchmark (FinRelBench) is introduced by the same authors, so the 90.72% figure may not transfer to real trading desks; boundary rules can block legitimate repairs or add friction without catching novel leakage modes; and the paper demonstrates violation containment only under its own controlled stress tests, not under production data or live-market conditions. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Provable Adversarial Detection: Prime Quantization meets Gromov--Wasserstein
item.description: The method replaces heuristic adversarial detectors (e.g., feature-density or statistics-based screens) with a detector that compares sample geometry across a CNN embedding space and a prime-quantized space, using Gromov–Wasserstein discrepancy with claimed separation guarantees. It adds per-inference cost: an extra embedding pass, a quantization mapping, and a GW-style distance computation, plus implementation complexity, without quantified latency or memory figures in the abstract. It can fail against adaptive attacks crafted to preserve geometry in both spaces, and its guarantees likely depend on the specific threat model, attack strength bounds, and embedding choices validated in the paper's experiments. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Hybrid GPU and Processing-Near-Memory Architecture with Shared DRAM for Efficient Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
item.description: DuoPD replaces GPU-side prefill-decode disaggregation and SM partitioning by executing full decoding on Processing-Near-Memory units in the HBM logic die while prefill runs on the GPU, sharing the HBM interface via TSV-level bandwidth allocation. The cost is entirely hardware-side: it requires custom PNM silicon, a new microarchitecture, and a hierarchical data-mapping scheme, with no software-only path to deployment. It can fail commercially if no memory vendor ships such parts, and technically if bandwidth sharing between GPU and PNM does not hold under real serving skew between prefill and decode load. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Holistic Buoyancy-Driven Cloud Native Resource Management
item.description: The method replaces static resource requests and prior workload profiling in Kubernetes scheduling with runtime 'buoyancy' signals that measure each workload's sensitivity to shared resources such as last-level cache and memory bandwidth, driving adaptive scheduling, node-local allocation, and limited rescheduling. It costs a Kubernetes-native control plane extension, continuous runtime instrumentation of workloads, and a multi-node cluster to provide rescheduling headroom, plus ongoing maintenance of the sensitivity-measurement framework. It can fail when buoyancy estimates are inaccurate or unstable under rapidly shifting workload mixes, when rescheduling triggers migration overhead or disruption, and its benefits are unproven outside the evaluated congestion regimes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
item.description: It replaces chunk-bounded speculative execution, where generation is truncated or restarted at each speech update, with periodic Thinker invocations that let ongoing reasoning and dispatched tool calls run to completion against the latest partial transcript and a shared results record. The cost is additional inference calls during listening (raising token/API spend), plus orchestration complexity for managing concurrent invocations and a shared state record. It can fail when partial transcripts mislead speculative tool calls into wasted or incorrect executions, and the paper notes final task quality effects are benchmark-dependent, so gains may not transfer to a given workload. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: AudioScorer: Learning Question-Aware Token Relevance for Large Audio Language Models
item.description: It replaces heuristic audio-token pruning (attention, similarity, temporal sampling) with a lightweight learned scorer that ranks tokens by relevance to the user question, distilled from the frozen LALM's answer-gradient saliency plus answer supervision. The cost is a one-time training/distillation stage that needs gradient access to a self-hosted frozen LALM, an added per-question scoring step in inference, and retained quality that depends on the chosen retention rate. It can fail on out-of-distribution questions or acoustic content where the scorer mis-ranks tokens, is unavailable for API-only models without gradients, and may degrade tasks that depend on dense temporal detail at aggressive retention. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The Control Layer Behind Rule-Following Agents Trading Across Market Conditions
item.description: The method replaces informal judgment of agent trustworthiness with reproducible trade-log tests that measure rule adherence (stops, targets, position limits, regime-conditional risk) before capital is committed. Cost is modest: the published trade snapshot, Bitcoin prices, and regime labels suffice to rerun the tests, but the methodology assumes agents that declare strategies and risk parameters upfront, and building equivalent instrumentation for a new agent is real engineering work. It can fail by producing false confidence: rule-following is shown to be orthogonal to profitability, sample sizes are small (2,627 positions, one unprofitable agent), and results are trade-level, not account-level returns. 1 independent implementation, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Generic On-Board AI Processing Chain for Earth Observation: From Application Development to Embedded Deployment and Mission-Level Orchestration
item.description: The method replaces ground-station processing of full downlinked scenes with an on-board chain of int8-quantized inference on FPGA, a reusable tiler-inference-mosaicer workflow, and unikernel-packaged steps orchestrated by a cloud-native on-board orchestrator. The cost is substantial embedded-engineering effort: model quantization and hardware porting, plus adoption of specialized unikernel packaging and orchestration infrastructure, none of which runs on a conventional GPU workstation. Adoption can fail through quantization-induced accuracy loss on new tasks, hardware-specific toolchain friction, and orchestration overhead on constrained space-grade compute. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement
item.description: VibeTraining-Bench replaces ad hoc manual tuning of data, trainer, and inference harness with a standardized benchmark that measures whether research agents can perform that co-design iteratively under a fixed budget. It costs substantial compute per run, since each episode requires repeated training and evaluation cycles inside isolated containers with anti-reward-hacking safeguards. It can fail to transfer: strong results by frontier research agents on this benchmark do not imply a small team with one 24 GB GPU can replicate the iterative training loops, and residual reward-hacking or overfitting to validation feedback remains possible. 2 independent implementations, 123 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Autonomous intelligence for mining productivity: a multi-agent AI approach to operational value creation
item.description: EI2ROC proposes a three-tier multi-agent architecture (LLM orchestrator plus specialised monitoring and production-capacity agents over an MCP-style tool interface) intended to replace manual, siloed supervision in mining Integrated Remote Operation Centres, alongside a six-dimension benchmarking framework for industrial agentic systems. It costs orchestration complexity, LLM inference cost and latency per decision in a safety-critical setting, and the paper itself marks most components as reference design or future work, with only preliminary cost and latency observations from one site. It can fail through orchestrator errors propagating to SCADA-connected actions, unmet real-time and regulatory-auditability requirements, and the absence of validated benchmarks for the industrial blind spot the paper identifies. 2 independent implementations, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: An Empirical Study of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
item.description: The recipe replaces full fine-tuning of MoE models (and adapters that bypass experts) with LoRA/DoRA applied directly to native expert weights, trained without a load-balancing auxiliary loss since no nonzero coefficient Pareto-dominated the zero baseline. Cost is limited to a small trainable-parameter budget (17% fewer than the module-bypass baseline) within a single-GPU fine-tuning run, plus a measured 3.2-point average downstream regression for the redesigned variant. Failure modes include expert routing drift degrading general-knowledge retention, results transferring poorly across the three studied backbones to other MoE architectures, and task-specific sensitivity to which experts and ranks are adapted. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CTLite: Lightweight Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Reusable Continuous-Time Summaries
item.description: CTLite replaces learned temporal encoders for irregular multivariate time series with a parameter-free continuous-time moment encoder whose summaries are cached and reused across optimization steps and repeated queries, leaving only a small damped-extrapolation plus low-rank cross-variable readout to train. It costs almost nothing in parameters or latency and runs on a single small GPU or even CPU-class hardware, but it adds a preprocessing and caching layer and its accuracy claim is only best-or-second-best rather than uniformly superior. It can fail where the moment-based local level and trend summaries are a poor fit for the dynamics, on datasets unlike the four evaluated benchmarks, or when histories change frequently enough to negate the reuse benefit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Coding Agents Outpace Review: Evaluating PRD-Driven Development in Mature Enterprise Repositories
item.description: PACE replaces ad hoc or issue-resolution-style evaluation of coding agents with evidence-based scoring of full PRD fulfillment against 750 expert-audited Code Points in mature repositories.
